name: Webaxys DC4 / SostraData La Souterraine
notes: Webaxys describes DC4 as a datacenter in La Souterraine, Creuse; Data Center Map profile notes SostraData was inaugurated in Creuse in September 2019.

name: DTiX Dijon
notes: Operator site lists the Dijon colocation datacenter at 24 rue de la Redoute, 21850 Saint-Apollinaire, with 120 racks across 3 rooms and 450 m2 IT area; APL announced its turnkey build for DTiX near Dijon.

name: Cogent Data Center - Dijon
notes: Cogent service-location list includes its Dijon data center at 41 Quai Gauthey, 21000 Dijon; Data Center Map lists about 2,345 sq ft and 0.25 MW.

name: Département de la Côte-d'Or sovereign data center
notes: Departmental official news says Côte-d'Or has a sovereign data center installed in the department, with 1.8 PB raw storage and 13 high-performance compute servers.

name: MAIF Chauray Data Center
notes: MAIF annual reporting describes construction of the new Chauray data center; EU Code of Conduct participant list includes MAIF's Chauray data center from 2021, supporting operational status.

name: Dordogne proximity data center project
notes: Le Journal des Entreprises reported a first proximity data center project in Dordogne, with possible installation within two years; details are limited/paywalled.

name: Hôtel du département Dordogne server/datacenter room
notes: FläktGroup case study describes a new datacenter/local server facility for the Hôtel du département in Périgueux, with 40-45 kW thermal load for the server extension.

name: nLighten Besançon MLH1 / Euclyde DC2
notes: nLighten official location page lists a Besançon edge data center with 300 m2 dedicated colocation and 1,200 kW power; facility traces back to the Neoclyde/Euclyde Besançon data center inaugurated in 2012.

name: Sesterce Valence / Rovaltain AI data center
notes: DCD reported Sesterce's EUR450m AI data center planned for Rovaltain/Valence with 40,000 GPUs. Later 2026 French reporting says the Grenoble administrative court suspended the building permit, so status is not construction.

name: Koesio Valence Data Center
notes: Data Center Map lists Koesio Valence at 53 avenue des Langories, Valence; public capacity details were not found.

name: Adista Romans-sur-Isère Data Center
notes: Data Center Map lists an Adista data center in Romans-sur-Isère in the Valence market; public capacity details were not found.

name: DATA4 Paris-Saclay Campus PAR01/PAR02
notes: DATA4 official Paris page lists PAR01 at 3 route de Marcoussis, Nozay; PAR02 at 15 rue Angiboust, Marcoussis; and cites 133 ha land reserve and 505 MW electrical reserve for its Paris campuses.

name: DATA4 PAR03 Nozay AI Campus
notes: DATA4 press release announced PAR03 in Nozay, Essonne, with 250 MW capacity, nearly 200,000 GPUs and heat reuse; earlier 2023 plan cited a 22 ha campus.

name: CloudHQ CDG Campus Lisses
notes: CloudHQ official campus page says the Lisses CDG campus has two fully permitted 74.4 MW IT-load buildings powered by a new 225 kV on-site substation; DCD reported ground was broken in late 2022.

name: Colt Paris South West Data Centre, Les Ulis
notes: Colt DCS official page lists its Les Ulis Paris South West data centre as operational, Tier 3 specification, with 24 MW IT power.

name: Colt Paris 5 & 6, Les Ulis
notes: Colt DCS official page says two proposed data centers at Les Ulis will provide 55 MW total; Colt's 2025 announcement says Paris 5 and 6 are scheduled on the Les Ulis site.

name: Éclairion Bruyères-le-Châtel AI/HPC data center
notes: Éclairion describes high-density AI colocation infrastructure; Île-de-France region said the Essonne center opened in early 2025. Data Center Map lists the Bruyères-le-Châtel campus at 120 MW.

name: Orange Normandy / Val-de-Reuil Data Center
notes: Orange's first Normandy facility at Val-de-Reuil is reported as 16,000 m2 with 5,000 m2 of computer rooms; Orange later referenced this Val-de-Reuil design when announcing similar facilities.

name: Orange Normandie 2 Val-de-Reuil
notes: Orange announced a new Normandie 2 data center in Val-de-Reuil: 16,000 m2 building with 5,000 m2 of IT rooms, part of more than EUR100m invested in the two Val-de-Reuil data centers.

name: EDF Noé Val-de-Reuil Data Center
notes: EDF says Noé is managed by its shared services division and provides high-capacity hosting for EDF applications; Enia project page lists the Val-de-Reuil project as delivered in 2010 with 16,000 m2 surface and 4,600 m2 server area.

name: Nation Data Center Val-de-Reuil
notes: DCD reported Nation Data Center announced plans for a second facility in Val-de-Reuil in the Eure department; no later operational confirmation found.

name: EDF Pacy-sur-Eure Data Center
notes: Data Center Map nearby-facilities data lists EDF Pacy-sur-Eure at 141 Rue Edouard Isambard; details are sparse, so confidence is aggregate-level only.

name: Orange Centre-Val de Loire / Chartres-Mainvilliers Data Center
notes: Orange announced a 16,000 m2 data center near Chartres with 5,000 m2 of IT rooms; L'Usine Nouvelle identifies the site as Mainvilliers, Eure-et-Loir, with EUR50m investment and service planned for late 2020.

name: C'CIN Chartres Innovation Numérique Datacenter
notes: C'CIN official page describes a local datacenter based in Chartres/Eure-et-Loir for hosting and securing business data; DC Mag's datacenter map lists C'CIN in department 28.

name: Grand Châteaudun data center study
developer: Communauté de communes du Grand Châteaudun
notes: Local outlet Intensité reported Grand Châteaudun approved EUR42,000 for a study to implant a future data center and said the territory was in the Top 35 projects announced at the AI summit.
